sources.title: UNESCO, Cities and Landmarks of Ma-in Old Kingdom
sources.note: Official heritage synthesis of Qarnawu, Yathill, irrigated Jawf settlements, trade, temples, and inscriptions.

sources.title: CNR, From city-state to kingdom: Ma-in in the eighth to sixth centuries BCE
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronology emphasizing debated origins, endogenous formation, Yathill confederation, and Sabaean rivalry.

sources.title: Archaeopress, Baraqish/Yathill excavations 1986-2007
sources.note: Open archaeological report covering stratigraphy, temples, domestic debris, economy, pottery, inscriptions, and environment.

sources.title: The Minaeans after Ma-in?
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reassessment of the kingdom collapse, later Minaic writing, and continuity after political change.

sources.title: UNESCO, Baraqish City Archaeological Site
sources.note: Official description of Yathill, its fortifications, trade and religious roles, Roman occupation, and later decline.

sources.title: UNESCO, Old Incense Trade Routes in Yemen
sources.note: Official route synthesis linking South Arabian capitals, caravan stations, temples, water works, and inscriptions.

sources.title: UNESCO Ma-in comparative and heritage dossier
sources.note: Detailed official documentation of Qarnawu planning, Baraqish canals, irrigated fields, dam, temples, and settlement landscape.

sources.title: Chronology of the Kingdom of Ma-in
sources.note: Scholarly reconstruction of thirty-nine rulers and the debated eighth-to-first-century BCE royal sequence.

sources.title: Minaeans in the Mediterranean: two inscriptions from Delos
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed edition, palaeographic dating, transliteration, translation, and attribution of the Delos altars.

sources.title: CNR Corpus of Central Minaic Inscriptions
sources.note: Scholarly corpus description for roughly 1,300 Minaic inscriptions from the South Arabian heartland.

sources.title: CNR Corpus of Marginal Minaic Inscriptions
sources.note: Scholarly corpus of Minaic inscriptions beyond the homeland, documenting trade stations and diaspora settings.

sources.title: CNR DASI digitization of pre-Islamic Arabian inscriptions
sources.note: Institutional account of the digital epigraphic corpus, metadata, languages, objects, texts, and research method.

sources.title: Open EpiHub, DASI resource
sources.note: CNR resource description covering editions, translations, bibliographies, word lists, object data, and geographic context.

sources.title: Dadanitic local calendar and Minaic contacts
sources.note: Peer-reviewed evidence for Minaic dating practice, mixed marriage, children, and interaction at Dadan.

sources.title: Family Organization in Pre-Islamic South Arabian Society
sources.note: University research on couples, descent, marriage, women, and family terms in South Arabian inscriptions.

sources.title: Minaeans at Hima: epigraphic corpus and implications
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of more than 150 caravan-route inscriptions, merchants, families, mobility, and cultural interaction.

sources.title: Semitic Documents on Wooden Sticks
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chapter on cursive documents, school exercises, archives, correspondence, contracts, and scribal education.

sources.title: Carved, Signed, Crossed Out: South Arabian wooden documents
sources.note: Scholarly account of Minaic and Sabaic letters, accounts, contracts, ritual texts, cancellation, and teaching samples.

sources.title: Bavarian State Library Ancient South Arabian inscriptions on wood
sources.note: Institutional collection of letters, legal and business documents, school exercises, and ritual texts on wooden sticks.

sources.title: Baraqish Area C: Economy, Trade, and the Environment
sources.note: Open archaeological chapter on plants, animals, seasonal floods, oasis ecology, trade evidence, and environmental change.

sources.title: Baraqish Area C: The Objects
sources.note: Open archaeological catalogue treating humble artifacts as evidence for behavior, work, and cultural life.

sources.title: Baraqish Area C: The Minaean Pottery
sources.note: Open specialist study of the excavated Minaean ceramic sequence, forms, contexts, and classification limits.

sources.title: Baraqish inscriptions and the Kingdom of Ma-in
sources.note: Open specialist chapter connecting Yathill inscriptions with political, urban, and regional history.

sources.title: Baraqish Area C: Setting, Stratigraphy, and Geoarchaeology
sources.note: Open excavation chapter on layered deposits, mudbrick structures, hearths, refuse, organics, and site formation.

sources.title: Sapienza, the Minaean necropolis at Baraqish
sources.note: University excavation report on pit graves, stelae, funerary customs, seasonal visitors, and evidence limits.

sources.title: Italian Archaeological Mission at Baraqish
sources.note: Mission history and excavation evidence for Yathill, Minaean temples, necropolis, chronology, and conservation.

sources.title: Excavation of the Athtar dhu-Qabd temple at Baraqish
sources.note: University excavation record for the massive hypostyle temple and its stratigraphic historical reconstruction.

sources.title: Harvard White-Levy project at Baraqish/Yathill
sources.note: Institutional project description of the second major city, temple publication, archives, and archaeological preservation.

sources.title: The South Arabian Kingdom of Ma-in: new Baraqish evidence
sources.note: Academy publication reassessing Ma-in through Italian excavations and epigraphic and settlement evidence.

sources.title: Unicode Old South Arabian character names
sources.note: Official character inventory used to normalize the published Delos transliteration into readable Unicode Musnad.

sources.title: Ancient Near Eastern Texts: South Arabian inscriptions
sources.note: University-hosted scholarly translations of Minaean building, family, land, taxation, and dedicatory inscriptions.

sources.title: Scuola Normale Superiore, Ancient South Arabian writing
sources.note: Academic reference on monumental and minuscule scripts, literacy levels, writing surfaces, and scribal institutions.
